comparator.institution: Wageningen University & Research / Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The current WUR handbook defines this 180-EC double-degree route for students from the SLU Forest and Landscape bachelor. It comprises a 144-EC common part (126 EC of compulsory SLU/WUR study plus an 18-EC WUR thesis), one 12-EC WUR specialisation and 24 EC of open electives. Society and Policy is selected by the official-order tie-break, using the first two listed 6-EC options. The SLU programme and syllabus corroborate the forestry-science, landscape, management, societal and field-study context.

routeSelection.basis: The double-degree target offers two equally formal 12-EC WUR specialisations, Society and Policy and Ecology and Conservation. Neither is clearly broader or less specialised, so the first current-handbook specialisation is selected before considering UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Forest landscapes, ecology & management
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines ecology, biodiversity and environmental systems with governance, economics, quantitative analysis and applied sustainability research, forming the broadest feasible UCR response to an interdisciplinary forest-and-landscape degree.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible response to Forest and Nature Conservation DD-SLU, combining biodiversity, ecology, climate and landscape systems with management, governance, economics, social evidence and research.
progression: Ecology, sustainability, politics, mathematics and social-science foundations precede conservation, evolution, public international law, environmental analysis, advanced ecology, governance and research. All prerequisites and term offerings pass; six 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Ecology, biodiversity & conservation science
alternatives.labelReason: The programme concentrates the shared scientific core in biodiversity, conservation biology, evolution, ecosystems, environmental systems, spatial evidence and field-oriented research.
alternatives.concept: A science-led route through ecology, biodiversity, conservation and environmental systems, using quantitative and spatial evidence to study forests and landscapes while retaining liberal-arts breadth.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest programme, this route replaces its sustained politics, law, economics, sociology and communication strand with deeper ecology, biology, Earth systems, sustainable farming and environmental field research. It clears the 30-EC distinctness floor.
progression: Biology, ecology, sustainability and quantitative foundations precede conservation, farming, earth observation, marine biology, environmental biogeochemistry and field research. All prerequisites and offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Nature policy, governance & societal change
alternatives.labelReason: The programme develops the societal specialisation through politics, law, sociology, economics, communication and sustainability governance, supported by ecology and environmental evidence.
alternatives.concept: A governance-led route focused on society, policy, law, economics, environmental justice and communication for forest, landscape and ecosystem-service decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the earlier programmes, this route replaces much of the ecology, organismal biology, conservation and landscape-science sequence with sustained politics, law, economics, sociology and communication. It clears the 30-EC distinctness floor against each.
progression: Sustainability, law, politics, economics, research and data foundations precede international law, public economics, advanced EU politics, governance, conflict analysis and applied sustainability research; prerequisites and term offerings pass.

core: Forest and landscape ecology, biodiversity, tree biology and ecosystem functioning
Management, design and conservation of forests, landscapes and ecosystem services
Human–nature relations, livelihoods, economics, policy and forest-landscape governance
Spatial, climate, quantitative and environmental evidence for landscape decisions
Field, interdisciplinary and independent research methods
An international two-country double-degree structure with open elective space
questions: How can forest biodiversity, landscapes and ecosystems be conserved and managed under climate change?
How can ecological and social evidence be combined in forest and landscape decisions?
How should conflicts over land, livelihoods and ecosystem services be governed?

selection.assessment: The closest programme combines forest-landscape ecology, environmental systems, management and society. The two formal WUR specialisations independently support a deeper Ecology and Conservation route and a Society and Policy route. All three are coherent, mechanically feasible and substantively distinct, so production stops at the maximum.

notes.text: The WUR–SLU double degree requires 126 EC of dedicated forest-and-landscape study plus an 18-EC thesis before its WUR specialisation and electives. UCR can combine ecology, biodiversity, environmental systems, governance and research into three defensible liberal-arts programmes, but it does not reproduce specialist tree biology, forestry and silviculture, landscape design and business, the two-country progression, or the same compulsory thesis and field structure.
